'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Kurdish–Turkish conflict (1978–present)|Kurdish–Turkish conflict]]
**[[Operation Claw-Eagle 2]]
***According to Turkish authorities, a [[Turkish military]] operation against [[Kurds|Kurdish]] [[Kurdistan Workers' Party|PKK]] fighters in [[Duhok Governorate|Duhok]], [[Iraq]], ends with the death of 48 PKK fighters, three Turkish soldiers, and 13 Turks who had been kidnapped by the PKK. [https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-turkey-iraq-security-idUSKBN2AE04Y (Reuters)]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
***Militants of the [[Islamic State's Central Africa Province]] [[Raid (military)|raid]] the town of Ndalya in the [[Ituri Province]] of the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], killing 11 civilians and three members of the [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|armed forces]]. [https://manilastandard.net/index.php/news/world-news/347060/dr-congo-militia-kills-11-civilians-army.html (AFP via ''Manila Standard'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maharashtra]]
*****The [[India]]n state of [[Maharashtra]] records 4,097 fresh infections after 39 days of no infections [https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/maharashtra-records-4k-covid-19-cases-after-39-days-health-experts-sound-alarm-101613362908989.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]]'s [[Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare|Ministry of Health]] officially approves the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]], three days after a government panel recommends its approval. This is the first [[government of Japan|government]]-approved [[vaccine]] in the country. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/02/14/japan-health-ministry-says-it-has-approved-pfizers-covid-19-vaccine.html (CNBC)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon]]
****[[Lebanon]] begins a [[vaccination]] campaign against [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], a day after the first 28,500 doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine]] arrived in the country. A doctor at [[Rafik Hariri University Hospital]] in [[Beirut]] is the first person to be vaccinated. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210214-lebanon-kicks-off-vaccinations-against-covid (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****The number of recovered COVID-19 patients in [[Pakistan]] surpasses 500,000. [https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/pakistan/covid-19-pakistans-total-recoveries-cross-500000-1.77197248 (''Gulf News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]]
****[[Saudi Arabia]] extends precautionary measures to reduce the spread of COVID-19, which restricts [[social gathering]]s to 20 people and suspends all events and parties, for another 20 days. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/saudi-arabia-extends-virus-restrictions-for-20-days/2144482 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Thailand]] reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant in a person who travelled from [[Tanzania]] and undergoes mandatory quarantine. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2068095/s-african-variant-hits-thailand (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
****In defiance to the [[Chamber of Deputies of the Czech Republic|Chamber of Deputies]], the [[Czech Republic|Czech]] [[Government of the Czech Republic|government]] re-declares a [[state of emergency]] for the next two weeks in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19, especially because of the emergence of the more contagious B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-czech-republic-coronavirus-pandemic-afe89f923934f5ae6fcee56509624f20 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****The [[France|French]] [[Direction générale de la Santé]] asks regional health agencies and hospitals to go into "crisis mode" beginning on February 18 in order to prepare for a possible increase in COVID-19 cases as a result of highly contagious [[variants of SARS-CoV-2]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/france-coronavirus-hospitals-crisis-mode-lockdown-b1802145.html (''The Independent'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
****[[Italian Minister of Health|Health Minister]] [[Roberto Speranza]] signs a provision that extends the ban on recreational skiing at resorts until March 5, effectively preventing ski resorts from opening tomorrow for the first time this season due to the spread of the UK variant and other variants of SARS-CoV-2. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/italy-blocks-monday-reopening-of-ski-slopes (AFP via RFI)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] surpasses 80,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1808936/world (''Arab News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
***[[Mexico]] receives a shipment of 870,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] from [[India]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/mexico-gets-over-8-lakh-astrazeneca-vaccine-doses-from-india-2370622 (NDTV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***[[New Zealand]] reports their first community cases of COVID-19 since January 24. The patients are a family from [[Auckland]].  [https://www.smh.com.au/world/oceania/new-zealand-reports-three-new-covid-19-local-cases-20210214-p572d3.html (''Sydney Morning Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda]]
***[[Rwanda]] begins a COVID-19 vaccination programme with limited supplies of [[World Health Organization|WHO]]-approved vaccines acquired through unnamed international partners, making it the first country in [[East Africa]] to begin its campaign. Healthcare workers and other high-risk groups will be the first to receive a vaccine. [https://www.reuters.com/article/healthcoronavirus-rwanda/rwanda-says-begins-covid-19-vaccinations-idUSL1N2KK0EO (Reuters)]
*[[Guinea]] declares a new [[Ebola]] epidemic after three people died and four others became ill in the country’s southeast. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/14/guinea-sees-first-ebola-deaths-since-2016 (Al Jazeera)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Cyprus-Israel relations]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
**[[President of Cyprus|Cypriot President]] [[Nicos Anastasiades]] and [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] announce an agreement to allow vaccinated travelers to travel between the countries without the need to [[quarantine]] in order to restore their countries' tourism industries. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/israel-cyprus-reach-tourism-deal-vaccinated-travelers-75892758 (ABC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**The leaders of the [[Military junta|junta]] issue warnings to the public against harboring fugitives at the same time that arrest warrants are issued. Among the fugitives is democracy activist [[Min Ko Naing]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/myanmar-coup-junta-fugitive-protesters-overnight-guests-14193522 (CNA)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Catalan regional election]]
**[[Catalonia|Catalans]] head to the polls to elect the new [[Parliament of Catalonia]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/spain-53-catalans-to-vote-in-test-of-separatist-movement/2021/02/14/5183b310-6e9d-11eb-a66e-e27046e9e898_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[Catalan independence movement|Pro-independence]] parties gain a majority of the votes for the first time, though voter participation was the lowest in history. The anti-independence [[Socialists' Party of Catalonia]], led by former [[Ministry of Health (Spain)|national Health Minister]] [[Salvador Illa]], wins the most seats for a single party. The [[far-right]] [[Vox (political party)|Vox]] places fourth and enters [[Parliament of Catalonia|Parliament]] for the first time, winning 11 seats. [[Citizens (Spanish political party)|Citizens]], who placed first in the [[2017 Catalan regional election|previous election]], falls to seventh and loses 30 seats. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/14/catalonia-regional-election-covid-voting (''The Guardian'')]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Peru]], [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**[[Peru]]'s [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Peru)|Foreign Minister]] [[Elizabeth Astete]] resigns amid an uproar over secret vaccination before the country receives one million doses for health workers. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/the_americas/perus-foreign-minister-quits-over-secret-vaccination/2021/02/14/ed38d65a-6f47-11eb-8651-6d3091eac63f_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2021 Kosovan parliamentary election]]
**[[Kosovo Albanians|Kosovans]] head to the polls to elect the new [[Assembly of Kosovo]]. The [[Vetëvendosje]] party is expected to gain most seats as it shows on exit polling data. [https://www.voanews.com/europe/kosovo-holds-early-parliamentary-election-120-seat-legislative-body%3Famp&ved=2ahUKEwi8nv-R4-ruAhW5ILcAHSc0CM0QFjAPegQIGRAB&usg=AOvVaw3_YD2CWITHsSrYINhanPCA&ampcf=1 (Voanews)] [https://amp.dw.com/en/kosovo-left-wing-opposition-set-to-win-election-exit-polls/a-56563753&ved=2ahUKEwi8nv-R4-ruAhW5ILcAHSc0CM0QFjAOegQIGBAB&usg=AOvVaw2aTUCZ07rXXMrhLOPMJzr2&ampcf=1 (DW)]
